steps.content: [Crime Scene]

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: We're very sorry about what happened to Nelson. But for the investigation, we'll need to bring him back to the Bureau, run some tests, and figure out what caused this. It'll help us move faster. I'll need your signature here, just confirming you're okay with the cooperation.
Not long after Chief leaves the crime scene, the victim's family finally arrives.

steps.speaker: Father
steps.content: Cooperation? Sure, of course. Whatever you need. We're law-abiding citizens, always have been. Important people like you show up, I'll tell you whatever you want to know.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Thank you, that's appreciated. Can you start by walking me through his recent behavior? Anything unusual, anything that stood out?

steps.speaker: Father
steps.content: Unusual...? Not really. He stayed in his room mostly. Didn't go out much. Didn't talk much. I've got my own life, he's got his. He's a grown man. I can't be following him around all day.

steps.speaker: Father
steps.content: Still, I've got to say... I dropped everything when I got the call. Had a deal in progress and put it all on hold. All this back and forth, the time, the lost work... it's not nothing, you understand. So I was wondering if there's any kind of compensation for that...
So that's what this is about. Wynn's pen pauses for a moment before she pulls herself back into work mode.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: ...Thank you for sharing all of that. I'll make sure your request gets passed up the chain. One more thing, you mentioned you and your son didn't talk much. Do you remember anything about his daily routine lately? Eating habits, sleep, anything he seemed really focused on?
Seeing that the young clerk isn't biting, the man tugs his belt up a little higher.

steps.speaker: Father
steps.content: What's there to remember? All day, chasing after some celebrity. The room is a disaster. Money vanishing into thin air. Never did a thing with his life. Honestly, some kids just turn out like that. Bad luck. Family gets stuck with it.

steps.speaker: Father
steps.content: Not that I'm here to air out family business. It's just... his situation's caused problems for everyone. Time off work, the stress of dealing with all this, especially since it's tied up with that idol nonsense... I was wondering about that compensation...

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: I'll pass your request along. Do you remember roughly when he started getting into all that? Any names he mentioned a lot, or events he went to?
This time, Wynn plays along smoothly.

steps.speaker: Father
steps.content: How would I know? I don't pay attention to that stuff. Look, I dropped everything the second I got the call. Canceled dinner. Put work on hold. Had to come all the way down here myself. So when you add up what this has cost me, I was wondering about—

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Compensation, yes. I really can't authorize that myself. But I will absolutely, definitely, without question pass along any reasonable requests you have.
Wynn is already one step ahead, answering before he can ask. The middle-aged man, caught off guard by being seen through so easily, turns defensive and angry.

steps.speaker: Father
steps.content: What's your deal, girl? If you can't actually do anything, what have we been standing here talking for? Who's in charge here? Get me someone who can actually make a decision.
He's about to shove past Wynn and barge into the cordoned-off area where Eugene and the guards are still investigating, when the radio at Wynn's side crackles to life at just the right moment.

steps.speaker: Communications
steps.content: There's no need to call anyone. The officer in front of you, Wynn, is in charge here.

steps.speaker: Communications
steps.content: This is your official notice: the Bureau has formally assumed jurisdiction over this case. All related material is now classified. The victim will be transported according to protocol. Family members are not permitted to interfere, obstruct, or enter the restricted area. As for the requests you've raised, none of them fall within our current procedures.

steps.speaker: Father
steps.content: You... you can't... why are you... what's that attitude of yours?!

steps.speaker: Communications
steps.content: Final reminder: cooperate with the officer in charge. Any further disruption, and you'll bear the consequences yourself.
Those few crisp words are finally enough to shut him down. He settles back into his seat with a sheepish expression and signs. Wynn exhales quietly in relief.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: You really saved me back there, Adjutant Nightingale. I was about ready to start pulling bills out of my own pocket.

steps.speaker: Communications
steps.content: It's fine. I heard from Chief that everyone split up, so I got a little worried.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Oh? Worried about which side, exactly? Our side, or the other side?
There's nothing but silence on the other end of the radio.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Don't worry. There are plenty of eyes on this case in Eastside. I'm sure nothing's going to go sideways...
No sooner have the words left her mouth than worried shouts ring out from behind her.

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: Cole, can you hear me?
[Suspenseful sound effect + Phanuel's singing]

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: Cole?
